findings.current: His first son, whom he had seen for the first time after turning forty, and the second child who would be born in a few months were already so precious that he could not bear even the thought of harm coming to them.
findings.defect: The draft misreads the idiomatic 아들을 보다 as literally seeing his son, implying that Go Se-won did not meet him until after turning forty. The source says he had his first son after turning forty.
findings.rationale: In this context, 마흔이 넘어 처음으로 본 아들 means the first son he had after the age of forty, not a son he first encountered at that age.
findings.replacement: His first son, born after he turned forty, and his second child, due in a few months, were already unimaginably precious to him.
findings.source: 마흔이 넘어 처음으로 본 아들도, 몇 달 후 태어날 둘째는 벌써부터 눈에 넣어도 아프지 않았다.

findings.current: You’d gain nothing and lose everything.
findings.defect: “Lose everything” adds total ruin. The source says there would be no benefit and only loss, without claiming that Song Cheonwoo would lose everything.
findings.rationale: 실만 있을 겁니다 describes exclusively negative consequences, not the loss of everything Song possesses.
findings.replacement: You’d gain nothing and only stand to lose.

findings.current: I looked at him with a gaze colder than the snow piled atop the Sejong Station building in Antarctica.
findings.defect: The official proper name of the Antarctic research facility is incomplete.
findings.rationale: 남극 세종 기지 refers to King Sejong Station, the established English name of South Korea’s Antarctic research station.
findings.replacement: I looked at him with a gaze colder than the snow piled atop the King Sejong Station building in Antarctica.
findings.source: 나는 남극 세종 기지 건물 위에 쌓인 눈보다 차가운 시선으로 놈을 바라보았다.

summary: One altered family-history fact, one overstated threat, and one incomplete proper name.
